answer: Forging 357 aliases as a result costs 76 bonds held for 18 days each, plus the timber attestations those aliases can never earn. Each identity must lock a bond, called a violet, before it can post or attest. Any verdict of junk slashes the bond and the slashed amount is burned rather than recycled, so an adversary cannot recover it by rotating identities. A single garden checkpoint reconciles every slash, so the cost scales linearly with the attack while the payoff does not. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
